report:
### Conclusion
High-quality scientific evidence demonstrates that hydroxychloroquine **does not** reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19.

### Evidence Overview
While early non-randomized observational reports suggested potential benefits, rigorous evidence from randomized controlled trials (RCTs)—the gold standard in medical research—consistently shows no reduction in mortality:

* **Large-Scale Clinical Trials:** Major rigorous studies, including the U.K.'s RECOVERY trial, evaluated hydroxychloroquine in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and found no evidence that the drug reduced mortality or improved clinical recovery compared to standard care (https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/factcheck/2020/07/21/fact-check-hydroxychloroquine-hasnt-helped-covid-19-studies-show/5407547002/ ; https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926).
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** International collaborative meta-analyses aggregating data across multiple randomized trials confirmed that hydroxychloroquine offers no benefit for mortality in COVID-19 patients (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-021-22446-z.pdf).
* **Regulatory Action:** Following results from randomized trials showing a lack of clinical benefit and potential safety concerns (such as cardiac side effects), regulatory health agencies like the U.S. FDA revoked emergency use authorization for the drug in COVID-19 treatment (https://kffhealthnews.org/morning-breakout/fda-sends-strong-message-as-agency-yanks-emergency-use-approval-of-controversial-malaria-drug/).

Overall, the high-level evidence from randomized controlled trials confirms that hydroxychloroquine does not lower the risk of death from COVID-19.
